title: 200Ah Battery Backup Time Calculator | Wattlyst
meta: See how many hours a 200Ah battery runs fans, lights, a fridge or a PC. Tubular and lithium, 12V or 24V, with a ready backup time table.
author: ali-ahmad

sections.h2: How to read the 200 Ah battery backup chart
p: The chart below uses the loads most Pakistani homes put on a UPS. One ceiling fan is about 80 W; two fans with LED lights about 200 W; a fan, lights and a TV about 300 W; a fridge with fans a few hundred watts more; and 1,000 W is the kind of load an iron, a microwave or a water motor adds. Each row is a 12 V tubular battery through a UPS at about 85% efficiency that draws about 30 W itself, using 50% of the battery.

Doubling the load almost halves the backup. To stretch a 200 Ah battery through a long outage, keep the TV and fridge off the UPS and run only fans and lights; the backup climbs from about 3 h 8 min to about 4 h 31 min.

A 150 Ah tubular battery at 12 V holds about 900 Wh of usable energy through a UPS. That is about 3 h 23 min at 200 W (two fans and lights); at 300 W with a TV added it drops to about three quarters of the 200 Ah figure of 3 h 8 min. The 150 Ah rows in the chart give the exact hours for each load.
If a 150 Ah battery is not enough, a second battery in series on a 24 V UPS doubles the energy, but you must change the bank voltage to 24 V in the calculator rather than entering the Ah twice.

faq.q: What is the 200 Ah battery backup time for one fan?
faq.a: About 9 h 40 min for one ceiling fan of about 80 W on a 12 V tubular battery through a UPS. An inverter fan or a DC fan draws less and runs longer.

faq.q: A 200 Ah battery gives how many hours?
faq.a: About 3 h 8 min at 300 W, about 4 h 31 min at 200 W and about 9 h 40 min at 80 W. The usable energy is fixed at about 1,200 Wh; the hours depend on the load.

faq.q: How much backup does a 200 Ah tubular battery give?
faq.a: The calculator uses 50% of the rating and a UPS at about 85% efficiency with about 30 W idle draw; the battery holds about 1,200 Wh, which gives about 3 h 8 min at 300 W. Many UPS units run the battery lower than that, which gives more hours but a shorter battery life.

faq.q: What is the backup of a 200 Ah lithium battery?
faq.a: About 6 h at 300 W for a 12.8 V LiFePO4 battery, nearly double the tubular figure, because lithium can use about 90% of its capacity. Switch the battery type to lithium above to see other loads.

faq.q: Can a 200 Ah battery run a 1,000 W load?
faq.a: Only for about 59 min, and less in practice because of the fast-discharge drop. The UPS must also be rated for 1,000 W or more; a typical home UPS of about a kVA cannot deliver it.

faq.q: Is there an inverter battery 200 Ah backup chart?
faq.a: Yes, the chart above lists one fan, two fans with lights, fan with lights and TV, fridge with fans and a 1,000 W load for 200 Ah and 150 Ah tubular batteries. Change the inputs for any other combination.

faq.q: How long does a 200 Ah battery run two fans and lights?
faq.a: About 4 h 31 min for a 200 W load on a 12 V tubular battery, which covers an evening of loadshedding with margin to spare.

faq.q: What is the backup time of a 150 Ah battery?
faq.a: About 3 h 23 min for two fans and lights (200 W), from about 900 Wh usable. For a fan, lights and TV expect three quarters of the 3 h 8 min that a 200 Ah battery gives.

key_facts: A 200 Ah, 12 V tubular battery stores about 1,200 Wh of usable energy for a UPS when used to the recommended 50% of its rating.
That 1,200 Wh runs one ceiling fan (80 W) for about 9 h 40 min, two fans with lights (200 W) for about 4 h 31 min, and a 1,000 W load for only about 59 min.
A 200 Ah lithium (LiFePO4) battery at 12.8 V gives about 6 h at 300 W, almost twice the tubular figure, because it can use about 90% of its capacity.
A 150 Ah tubular battery gives three quarters of the backup of a 200 Ah battery at the same load: about 3 h 23 min at 200 W.
mistakes: Counting the full 200 Ah. A tubular battery should only be taken to about 50%; going deeper every day cuts its life to a year or two.
Entering the Ah of two batteries added together. Two batteries in series on a 24 V UPS keep the same Ah and double the volts; set the bank voltage instead.
Forgetting the inverter loss. The UPS turns only about 85% of the battery energy into AC power.
Expecting the chart figure at a 1,000 W load. The label Ah is rated over about twenty hours; drained in an hour a tubular battery gives noticeably less.

ups-idle.name: UPS / home inverter idle draw (no load)

fields.name: ah
fields.label: Battery capacity
fields.hint: 150 Ah and 200 Ah are the common Pakistani tubular sizes. Enter the Ah of one battery, not the total of a bank.

fields.name: load_w
fields.label: Load
fields.hint: Total watts on backup. A ceiling fan is under a hundred watts; a fridge, TV and several fans together are a few hundred.

fields.name: inverter_eff
fields.label: Inverter efficiency
fields.hint: As a decimal. A basic home UPS is about 0.85; a good hybrid inverter about 0.9.

fields.name: idle_w
fields.label: Inverter idle draw
fields.hint: What the UPS or inverter uses itself, even with nothing plugged in (no-load current × battery volts on its label). Not counted when inverter efficiency is one (a DC load).

fields.name: dod
fields.label: Usable depth of discharge
fields.hint: As a decimal: 0.5 means half the battery. Leave blank to use the value for your battery type.

how.tpl: {{in.ah}} Ah × {{in.volts|1}} V × {{out.dod|pct}} usable = {{out.stored_wh|int}} Wh in the battery. The battery gives {{in.load_w}} W ÷ {{out.inverter_eff|pct}} inverter efficiency + {{out.idle_w}} W the inverter draws itself = {{out.battery_w|1}} W. {{out.stored_wh|int}} Wh ÷ {{out.battery_w|1}} W = {{out.hours|2}} hours, about {{out.hours|hm}}.
how.text: 200 Ah × 12 V × 50% usable = 1,200 Wh in the battery. The battery gives 300 W ÷ 85% inverter efficiency + 30 W the inverter draws itself = 382.9 W. 1,200 Wh ÷ 382.9 W = 3.13 hours, about 3 h 8 min.

msg.load_must_be_positive: Enter a load greater than 0 watts.
msg.bank_voltage_not_multiple_of_battery: The bank voltage must be a whole multiple of the battery voltage (for example 24 V = 2 × 12 V).
msg.n_parallel_must_be_whole: Number of parallel strings must be a whole number.
msg.n_series_must_be_whole: Number of batteries in series must be a whole number.
msg.surge_w_required: Enter the starting (surge) watts of your load, or leave both surge fields blank.
msg.surge_rating_w_required: Enter the UPS surge rating from its label, or leave both surge fields blank.
msg.appliance_unknown: Pick an appliance from the list, or choose Custom and enter its watts.
msg.load_exceeds_ups_rating: This load is more than the UPS can deliver (VA × power factor). Choose a bigger UPS or reduce the load.
msg.surge_exceeds_ups_rating: The starting surge is above the UPS surge rating. Choose a bigger UPS or remove the motor load.
msg.forecast_unavailable: The live forecast is not available right now, so a typical day is shown. Try again later.
msg.typical_used: Blank boxes in your list use the typical value for that appliance (its listed watts and hours a day, quantity 1). Type your own numbers for an exact result.
msg.internal_non_finite: These numbers are outside a realistic range. Please check your inputs.

examples.title: 200 Ah battery backup time for one fan
examples.text: One ceiling fan at 80 W: 200 Ah × 12 V × 50% = 1,200 Wh, ÷ 124 W from the battery = about 9 h 40 min, a whole night.

examples.title: 200 Ah battery for two fans and lights
examples.text: Two fans with a few LED bulbs are about 200 W. 1,200 Wh ÷ 265 W from the battery = about 4 h 31 min on a 12 V tubular battery.

examples.title: 200 Ah battery for a 1,000 W load
examples.text: 1,200 Wh ÷ 1,206 W from the battery = about 59 min. The UPS draws about a hundred amps from the battery at this load, and a tubular battery drained this fast gives less than its label Ah, so the real figure is shorter.

examples.title: 200 Ah lithium battery backup
examples.text: 200 Ah × 12.8 V × 90% = 2,304 Wh usable. At 300 W that is about 6 h, roughly double the tubular figure for the same load in the chart.

examples.title: 150 Ah battery for two fans and lights
examples.text: 150 Ah × 12 V × 50% = 900 Wh, ÷ 265 W from the battery = about 3 h 23 min.

content.answer: A 200 Ah, 12 V tubular battery gives about 3 h 8 min of backup for a 300 W load (a fan, lights and a TV) through a home UPS, using the safe 50% of its capacity. Backup hours = Ah × volts × usable depth of discharge ÷ (load watts ÷ inverter efficiency + the inverter's idle draw); the chart below shows common loads.

lines: Ah = battery capacity in amp hours
P_idle = the inverter's own draw with no load (from its label; none for a DC load)

content.safety: Keep tubular batteries in a ventilated place away from sparks, use cables and fuses rated for the UPS current, and have a licensed electrician connect the UPS to house wiring.
